title: (No AI) xAI is buying out homeowners who promise not to sue over data center noise
author: Emma Roth
content:
![A photo of xAI’s Southaven, Mississippi data center](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/gettyimages-2289399619.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

xAI’s Southaven, Mississippi data center. | Photo by Brandon Dill / AFP via Getty Images

A subsidiary of Elon Musk's xAI is offering to buy up homes in a Mississippi neighborhood, as long as residents don't join a lawsuit targeting the company's nearby data center and power plant, [according to a report from _The Guardian_](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/28/datacenter-noise-lawsuit-elon-musk-mississippi). A realtor going door-to-door in the Southaven neighborhood reportedly told one resident that xAI plans to purchase 418 homes, adding that 18 homeowners already have plans to sell. People who rent homes in the area report [they're already being forced out](https://wreg.com/news/local/xai-memphis/spacexai-data-center-expansion-in-southaven-forces-renters-out/), with 60 days' notice after their landlords agreed to sell.

A recent report from the [_Mississippi Free Press_](https://www.mississippifreepress.org/xai-moves-to-buy-out-southaven-residents-who-agree-not-to-sue-it-over-power-plant-noise-letter-shows/) includes a letter received by several households rec …

title: (No AI) Voters in Texas agree: They hate data centers
author: Justine Calma
content:
![Greg Abbott, Gina Hinojosa, James Talarico, and Ken Paxton in the shape of Texas with glitchy effects.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/268813_TEXAS_DATA_CENTERS_CVirginia.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Ask Texas NAACP president Gary Bledsoe what it's been like to see data center developers descend upon Austin and its surrounding suburbs and he can rattle off project after project facing opposition from locals.

There's the [fight in Taylor](https://spectrumlocalnews.com/tx/south-texas-el-paso/news/2026/10/05/taylor-data-center-investigation) over plans to build a data center at a site that's supposed to be a park. Temple, around 40 miles away, is another sore spot, Bledsoe says. The mayor and City Council members there face [recall](https://spectrumlocalnews.com/tx/south-texas-el-paso/news/2026/08/04/recall-petition-in-response-to-data-centers) [attempts](https://www.kcentv.com/article/news/local/temple-recall-effort-against-mayor-davis-and-council-members-falls-short-of-needed-signatures/500-70af88ad-4e48-4bce-8d0a-2c8ff2e7fc50) over data center developments. And some 30 miles outside of Austin, San Marcos became the first [city in all of Texas to ban data centers](https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/business/2026/06/30/texas-data-centers-san-marcos-ban-opposition-poll-state-regulations/90750494007/).

Nowhere in the world are data centers growing more explosively than …
